the hair follicle is a good model for the study of radiation damage induced by heavy particles, that the damage to this structure increases with the increasing l.e t. of the helium ion beam and that this damage is dose dependent.

a) the response of hair follicles to the increasing l.e,t. of the helium ion beam is not homogeneous, b) there is a clear dose threshold for hair follicle damage and that c) the response to the increasing l,e,t. is not linear.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods of radiation damage analysis and with the study of radiation effects on biological systems.
the development of a new method for the evaluation of the in vivo response to heavy particle irradiations.
the study of the biological effects produced by the variable l.e. t. of a beam of helium ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hair follicle is a very sensitive system for the detection of radiation damage.
the biological damage is a function of l.e.t.
the damage to the hair follicle increases with the increase of the l.e.t.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hair follicle damage is a function of the l.e.t. at which the sample has been irradiated.
the hair follicle response to heavy ion irradiation is a function of the ion l.e.t. and that the hair follicles are more radiosensitive than the skin.
a single helium ion beam can be used to study the effects of heavy particle irradiation in the biological systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the damage to hair follicles increases with increasing l.e.t., with the highest damage occurring at the lowest l.e.t.
